clue.text: A snort from a person who should win…

definitions.meaning: a snort is a quick drink of spirits, slang for a swift tot
in a race the fast runner is the one expected to come first

explanation.surface: A racegoer grunts at the favourite, setting up the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue: the fast runner should win a race on the flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift drink taken in haste is slang for a snort; a fast competitor is the one tipped to win.

clue.text: … anything but a steeplechase

parts.note: a steeplechase has fences and ditches, so the opposite kind of horse race is run over level ground with no jumps

explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues the previous one; a steeplechase is a British jumps race, so its opposite is run with no obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over level ground with no jumps is the opposite of a steeplechase with its fences.

clue.text: Maybe a plug for a novel transcriber

definitions.meaning: a plug fitting may be a device letting one connector fit another socket
someone who turns a novel into a play or film reworks it for a new medium

explanation.surface: Perhaps a publicity mention helps someone who copies out a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A converter fitting lets a plug fit a foreign socket, and a screenwriter who reworks a book for the screen is the same word.

clue.text: French bitterness over return of the Channel Islands

parts.note: gall means bitterness or rancour

indicators.note: return of tells us to read the islands' abbreviation backwards

parts.note: CI is the standard abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Resentment in France at the handing back of Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic is an adjective for things of France, from the Latin name for ancient Gaul.

clue.text: I go astray in South American mountain chain

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South
to err is to go astray or wander from the right path

explanation.surface: A traveller gets lost among the peaks of the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one description of the range, but it splits into S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged range of peaks, from the Spanish word for saw.

clue.text: Ran a West London borough by chicanery

parts.note: doubled can mean ran at the double, moving fast
Ealing is a borough of West London

explanation.surface: Someone ran an outer London council by underhand means.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a London borough in the west of the city, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-faced conduct, saying one thing and doing another, is chicanery or deceit.

clue.text: Start constructing a rhomboid to provide an analogy

definitions.meaning: a rhomboid has two pairs of matching opposite sides, so building one begins by drafting a matching line
to offer a comparison between two similar things

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson segues into a lesson in comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally sketching a line beside another, figuratively making a comparison between similar cases.

clue.text: Giving up crime but not turning the corner

definitions.meaning: an ex-convict who stays honest is said to have reformed
carrying on ahead rather than turning at the junction

explanation.surface: A reformed crook is told not to take the bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for an offender leading an honest life, and literally continuing ahead without a bend.

clue.text: Mother with Caledonian charm

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Caledonia is the old name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A mum from north of the border has winning ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charm' reads as allure, but here means a lucky token.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky emblem or talisman, an object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Sort of glass I had taken to the Arctic circle

parts.note: polar describes regions like the Arctic
a circle is shaped like the letter O
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone took a drinking glass on an expedition inside the Arctic Circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arctic circle' reads as one place, but splits into the polar region and a ring shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Polarising sheet material is used in sunglasses lenses, a kind of tinted glass.

clue.text: Erotic excitement in a brute

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the phrase a brute, running across its two words

explanation.surface: A lustful thug is aroused.
explanation.definitionFit: The rut is the season of sexual arousal in deer and other animals.

clue.text: Temple where father is filled with a divine spirit

indicators.note: is filled with means the word for father is opened and the other pieces packed inside

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a god is a divine being or spirit

explanation.surface: Dad has a religious experience at a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine or place of worship.

clue.text: Switching centre for trading institution

definitions.meaning: a telephone switching centre connects calls between lines
a stock market or similar place where goods and shares are traded

explanation.surface: A firm moves headquarters to a market building.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephone hubs and stock markets are both called by this word, from swapping connections or goods.

clue.text: Say Hi and hurry!

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the greeting and take the word that sounds the same

parts.note: hi is the informal greeting

explanation.surface: A greeting and an urging to rush along.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an archaic verb meaning to hasten or go quickly.

clue.text: Frisked a South African revolutionary

parts.note: Cape is the province of South Africa round Cape Town, used as an adjective for things from there
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel from South Africa was searched by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisked' means searched in the surface, but here it means skipped about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk is to gambol or leap about playfully, the same as to caper.

clue.text: Put one's oar in and create an argument

definitions.meaning: literally dip a blade into water to propel a boat
start a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A busybody interferes and starts a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's oar in' is an idiom for interfering, but here it is taken literally as rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Propelling a boat with oars, and a noisy quarrel, rhyming with cow.

clue.text: Excessive weight is dispersed yet sob

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered widely, so the letters of the surrounding words are spread into a new order

parts.note: the fodder as printed, less one of its two S's, which the printed clue has spare

explanation.surface: Someone weeps as their extra pounds scatter at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'dispersed' sits between its fodder; as printed IS YET SOB has one S too many, so one S must be dropped to give the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being severely overweight is the medical condition of excess body fat.

clue.text: Showed a pale face how vegetables are par-boiled

definitions.meaning: went white with fear or shock
cooks briefly scald vegetables in boiling water

explanation.surface: A cook goes white while preparing the greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To go white with shock, and to scald food briefly in boiling water, share one verb.

clue.text: So a nicer set is needed for a drama plot

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters of so a nicer are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A friendlier stage set is required for the storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like stage scenery, but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a play or film.

clue.text: Climbing arachnid with large middle and gaudy mouth

indicators.note: with large middle means the abbreviation is placed in the centre of the other word
climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a spider is an eight-legged arachnid
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A spider crawls up across a garishly painted mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns SPIDER into REDIPS, and 'middle' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lips painted bright scarlet with lipstick make a showy mouth.

clue.text: Difficult battle ahead of English computing equipment

indicators.note: ahead of means these pieces come before the abbreviation

parts.note: hard means difficult
war is battle or armed conflict

explanation.surface: A tough fight precedes England's arrival in the tech world.
explanation.definitionFit: The physical machinery of a computer system, as opposed to its programs.

clue.text: Pipe construction in some French port

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters go inside the French word

parts.note: de is French for some, as in du or de la

indicators.note: construction means the letters of pipe are built into a new shape

explanation.surface: Building a pipeline in a French harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' is the anagram signal for 'Pipe', and 'in' puts the result inside the French for some; Dieppe is a Normandy port, so 'French' does double duty in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a Channel port in Normandy, a ferry terminal for crossings from England.

clue.text: What the wrongdoer should make at noon

definitions.meaning: an offender should make reparation for harm done
noon is when the morning, abbreviated as am, finishes

explanation.surface: An offender must put things right at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: AM is the abbreviation for morning; at noon the morning ends, read as a phrase of two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation for wrongdoing, and a pun: the morning (am) ends at twelve.

clue.text: Tarzan was a physical fitness fanatic

definitions.meaning: the jungle hero raised by apes
read as ..., someone keen on physical education

explanation.surface: The jungle hero was a gym enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school sports lesson, so a fitness fan is read as a PE man.
explanation.definitionFit: The jungle hero raised by great apes is a wild human, and a gym devotee is punningly a PE fan.

clue.text: Brown is to press for payment

definitions.meaning: a dull greyish-brown colour, as of a horse
to demand repayment of a debt insistently

explanation.surface: Brown is said to be chasing a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' might suggest the former UK prime minister Gordon Brown, but it is just the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull greyish-brown horse colour, and to badger a debtor for money.

clue.text: Wood hyacinth for a stage girl

definitions.meaning: a woodland flower with ...-shaped blooms
the ... Girls were a famous troupe of dancers at the Lido in Paris

explanation.surface: A woodland flower is the stage name of a showgirl.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bluebell Girls were a celebrated troupe of tall chorus dancers in Paris cabaret.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring woodland flower, and a member of a famous Paris dance troupe.

clue.text: What one must pay for electricity supply

definitions.meaning: a fee or price demanded
a store of electrical energy, as in a battery

explanation.surface: The bill one must settle for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A price or fee, and the amount of electrical energy stored or carried.

clue.text: I spotted peril developing for butterfly minded student

indicators.note: developing means taking a new form, so the letters are worked into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone sees danger approaching for a student of butterflies.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies moths and butterflies, an entomologist of that order.
